column1: # npm package versions that a GitHub or OpenSSF malware advisory, or the research post an
# incident links to, names as malware. One line each, tab separated.
#   version   the exact version, or * when every version of that name is malware
#   Axios, Bitwarden, OpenSearch, tensorlake and Injective: the versions their advisories name.
#   TanStack wave, May 2026: every npm version in the affected-packages list of Wiz's post on it,
#     each also named by a GitHub or OpenSSF malware advisory: the 42 @tanstack packages
#     (GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx) and the packages the worm spread to (tanstack), the @mistralai builds
#     payload could not run (mistral, uipath: versions to update), and OpenSearch
#     (GHSA-298w-vvm4-ww55). Not the @cap-js, mbt and intercom-client versions Wiz's list also
#     names, which were compromised in April.
#   Mastra, June 2026: the 89 @mastra packages, mastra and create-mastra that GitHub lists, and
#     easy-day-js 1.11.22, which Socket says each of the 141 compromised @mastra packages pulled in.
#   keyv, August 2026: keyv 6.0.0, the nine cacheable versions and ecto 5.0.1, which carried the
#     payload (keyv), and the 19 @keyv 6.0.0 builds (keyvscope): Socket says they were published without
#     the install hook, but GitHub's malware advisories say a machine that installed one is compromised,
#     and those govern. Not the packages the worm spread to after that.
#   SANDWORM_MODE, February 2026: the 19 malicious packages of Socket's list (sandworm) and the
#     four it calls sleeper packages, not malicious yet (sandsleep: versions to update).
# Not listed: the AntV and Red Hat waves. tensorlake's advisory also lists every version, but
#! skip tensorlake * the advisory also lists every version, but names only 0.5.144 as malicious
